newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Kiwi dollar closes trapped in narrow range.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi dollar closes trapped in narrow range.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed barely changed on Wednesday after trading in a narrow ten point range during the day.

"It has been reasonably active but in all honesty we are not breaking out of any ranges. A ten point range on the day is by anybody's standards quite narrow. The kiwi is a boring currency right now," a chief bank dealer said.
The NZ dollar closed at US$0.6885/92, while the Trade Weighted Index finished at 67.63 against a 67.62 opening.
"The range on the day was 0.6887/97 and it is closing around 0.6887/90," the chief dealer said.
There was early buying on the back of a stronger Australian dollar but the kiwi fell back as sellers from Asia came in.

"Just as we got to the highs we saw some Asian selling, mainly out of Japan, and that knocked the kiwi back to the 0.6890 level and that is where it has settled for the remainder of the afternoon," the chief dealer said.
He said the key for the debt market and the currency would be the June 26 Budget and the RBNZ's monetary policy statement on June 27.
"There is plenty of action elsewhere with the Aussie and the U.S. and the kiwi unfortunately is taking a bit of a backseat."
Dealers saw a support level of 0.6870/80 with stern resistance around the figure and 0.6915 and an overnight range between 0.6875 and 0.6905 in offshore trading.
